title: Draft consumer plan after ADR-001 capability manifest convention
body: ADR-001 and the initial `capabilities/*.json` manifests shipped as documentation + schema in commit c3c2059. This plan is the narrow consumer pass that gives that convention machine-checkable effect without adding a new product surface. Scope is intentionally limited to loader/schema validation, doctor/prereq metadata binding, adapter registry capability_id binding, external_refs capability binding, and an advisory required-capabilities sidecar at plan lock. No `dontpanic capabilities` CLI, no automatic adapter installation, no plugin marketplace, no per-service setup wizard. Active plan amendments (Firebase, External Integrations, OpenClaw) may cite capability manifests before this plan lands; those citations are documentation-only until F001 validates manifests and later features wire consumers.

title: F001 lands loader-first; jsonschema becomes runtime dependency
body: F001 implements only the loader/schema-validation foundation: `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/capabilities.py` discovers `capabilities/*.json`, validates each manifest against the checked-in `claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/capability.schema.json`, enforces id == filename stem, validates repo-relative setup_doc target files, exposes lookup by id/category, and fails loud on duplicate ids. This does not add a `dontpanic capabilities` CLI and does not make doctor/init/adapters consume manifests yet. Because the loader is now a core contract rather than a CI-only check, `jsonschema>=4.0` is added to runtime dependencies in pyproject.toml. Verification: focused F001 tests pass (9 passed); ruff check passes for the loader/tests/pyproject; ruff format --check passes for the loader/tests.
